script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

A bustling coffee shop. CUSTOMERS chatter, baristas work. In the corner, JANE, mid 30s, looks at her laptop. Disappointed, she closes it. She glances around, spotting RICHARD, mid 40s, entering.

RICHARD
(smiling)
Hey, Jane. Long time no see.

JANE
(surprised)
Richard? Is that you?

Jane stands, they hug. They catch up.

JANE
It's been so long. What have you been up to?

RICHARD
Same old thing. Work, kids, life. But enough about me. What have you been up to?

JANE
Oh, not much. Just trying to make it as a writer.

RICHARD
(impressed)
Wow, really? I didn't know that. I always thought you had a great imagination.

JANE
(smiling)
Thank you. I've been working on a new story. I'll send it to you when it's finished.

They exchange contact info.

INT. JANE'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Jane sits at her laptop, typing away. She saves the document, looks up and notices a picture of her and Richard from college. A smile forms on her face.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Jane sits with Richard, presenting him with her manuscript. He reads intently, occasionally looking up with a curious expression.

RICHARD
(impressed)
This is... amazing, Jane. I had no idea you had this in you.

Jane beams with pride.

INT. PUBLISHER'S OFFICE - DAY

Jane and Richard, both dressed up, sit across from a PUBLISHER.

PUBLISHER
I've read your manuscript, Jane. It's quite unique and I'd be happy to publish it.

Jane and Richard exchange excited glances.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Jane, now a published author, sits with Richard. They celebrate with coffee and pastries.

JANE
(grateful)
I couldn't have done it without you, Richard.

RICHARD
(smiling)
You had it in you all along, Jane. I just helped you see it.

INT. BOOKSTORE - DAY

Jane signs copies of her book. A line of fans waits patiently. Richard looks on with pride.

INT. JANE'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Jane sits on her couch, looking at her laptop. She sees a notification that Richard has read her latest manuscript. She opens it, smiles and types him a thank you note.

FADE OUT.

THE END
